title: TypeScript SDK: declarative union mappers and streaming-friendly Zod/JSON-Schema helpers
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a declarative, ergonomically friendly approach in the TypeScript SDK for mapping discriminated unions produced by Redwood models to strong runtime validators and JSON-Schema artifacts, with first-class support for streaming responses. This ticket contains the design decisions, implementation tasks, and acceptance criteria for the runtime and codegen work. We must keep the public SDK ergonomics simple for app devs while enabling advanced streaming use-cases and safe progressive parsing.
acceptance_criteria: Type generation produces union alias metadata (alias names + discriminator keys) alongside existing interfaces so consumers can import union helpers without handwritten types.

Runtime: the SDK exposes `createUnionMapper` that maps raw pieces (possibly partial during streaming) into discriminated runtime branches and returns a typed wrapper that integrates with Zod transforms.

Streaming ergonomics: incremental parse helpers (`progressiveParse` + `zodProgressiveTransform`) that validate partial chunks and surface typed events for the consumer (e.g., 'partial', 'complete', 'error').
JSON-Schema: a companion JSON-Schema emitter that can generate per-variant schemas and an overall oneOf wrapper for use in server-side contract tests and quick validations.
Backwards compatibility: existing ts-sdk user code that relies on current generated types remains working; any breaking changes are behind opt-in flags in codegen config.

Automated tests (unit + integration) demonstrating streaming union resolution across three real-world examples: chat function-calling shapes, multi-modal response types, and embedding/metadata union shapes.
tasks: Design: finalise the union alias metadata format for typegen (fields: aliasName, discriminatorKey, tagMap) and publish spec in docs/ts-sdk-unions.md
Codegen: update ts-sdk typegen to emit alias metadata JSON adjacent to .d.ts output and add `--emit-union-metadata` flag
SDK runtime: implement createUnionMapper API with streaming-aware transition logic and retry-safe resolution
Zod helpers: add `zodProgressiveTransform` and `zodVariantSchema` helpers to @redwood/ts-sdk-zod package
JSON-Schema emitter: implement a generator that consumes union metadata and outputs `oneOf` wrapper and per-variant schemas
Examples: three example projects under /examples/ts-sdk/unions: chat-function-calls, multimodal-responses, embedding-metadata
Tests: streaming simulation harness for partial chunks + property-based test for discriminator collisions
Docs: migration guide + API docs + short blog-like explainer for developer portal
Review & rollout: internal beta, migrate internal integration test suites, and opt-in toggle for users
decisions: Use alias metadata file (JSON) emitted by typegen instead of encoding everything into types to keep runtime small and avoid type-only artifacts needing TS reflection
Prefer Zod for runtime validation to match existing ts-sdk patterns; provide JSON-Schema export as convenience for third parties and contract tests
Streaming progressive validation will favour permissive 'partial' states: partial chunks are allowed to be validated against looser schemas and emit typed events until final validation succeeds
Expose structured helpers at `@redwood/ts-sdk/streaming-unions` so we can iterate without changing the core client import surface
Opt-in features behind config: `emitUnionMetadata: true` and `streamingUnionMode: 'progressive'` to avoid surprising existing users
